Pokémon TCG AI Battle · Public Replay Study

The Anatomy of a Winning Turn

What high-rated agent–deck systems do differently before they attack.
16 teams · 160 player-perspectives · 1,052 turns · 6,815 strategic actions
> **TL;DR.** High-rated systems do not merely attack more. In this snapshot, they build **deeper turns**: about **+1.9 strategic actions per turn** and **+2.0 pre-attack actions** versus the low-rated cohort. Draw is the clearest individual separator, but exact-deck checks suggest the broader pattern is sequencing quality—not one card or one motif. This notebook follows the action chain `draw → search → evolve → attach → gust → attack` through public replays. It is descriptive, auditable, and deliberately avoids causal claims."},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":1,"id":"d152b620","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-08-02T00:05:23.716799Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-08-02T00:05:23.716595Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-08-02T00:05:24.747894Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-08-02T00:05:24.747367Z"}},"outputs":[],"source":"import sankey_paths(frame): paths = [] for seq in frame.sequence: tokens = [x.strip() for x in seq.split("→")] if "ATTACK" not in tokens: continue pre = tokens[:tokens.index("ATTACK")] if len(pre) == 0: stages = ["DIRECT", "READY", "READY"] elif len(pre) == 1: stages = [pre[0], "READY", "READY"] elif len(pre) == 2: stages = [pre[0], pre[1], "READY"] else: stages = [pre[0], pre[1], pre[-1] if len(pre) == 3 else "…"] paths.append(["START"] + stages + ["ATTACK"]) return paths def sankey_trace(frame, cohort, color): paths = sankey_paths(frame) labels, label_index = [], {} def node(stage, value): key = f"{stage}:{value}" if key not in label_index: label_index[key] = len(labels) labels.append(value) return label_index[key] links = {} for path in paths: for stage, (left, right) in enumerate(zip(path, path[1:])): key = (node(stage, left), node(stage + 1, right)) links[key] = links.get(key, 0) + 1 source, target, value = zip(*[(s, t, v) for (s, t), v in links.items()]) node_colors = [color if label in {"START", "ATTACK"} else "#CBD5E1" for label in labels] rgba = "rgba(37,99,235,.24)" if cohort == "high" else "rgba(245,158,11,.25)" return go.Sankey( arrangement="snap", node=dict(label=labels, Each cell is the raw high-minus-low difference in the probability that a turn contains the motif. It is a descriptive map, not a set of independent hypothesis tests."},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":8,"id":"bda3906d","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-08-02T00:05:27.799564Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-08-02T00:05:27.799465Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.0284Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.027841Z"}},"outputs":[],"source":"phase_order = ["early", "mid", "late"] motif_order = ["has_draw", "has_search", "has_evolve", "has_attach", "has_gust", "has_attack"] phase = turns.groupby(["cohort", "phase"])[motif_order].mean() matrix = ((phase.loc["high"] - phase.loc["low"]).loc[phase_order, motif_order].T * 100) matrix.index = [m.replace("has_", "").upper() for m in matrix.index] matrix.columns = [x.title() for x in matrix.columns] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 5.2)) sns.heatmap(matrix, annot=True, fmt="+.1f", cmap=sns.diverging_palette(35, 240, s=75, l=52, as_cmap=True), center=0, linewidths=1.5, linecolor="white", cbar_kws={"label": "High − low (pp)"}, ax=ax) ax.set_title("Motif-rate differences by game phase", loc="left") ax.set_xlabel("Focal-player phase") ax.set_ylabel("") finish_mpl(fig, "04_phase_heatmap")"},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"8735eafc","metadata":{},"source":"The draw gap begins immediately and persists. High-rated systems also attach more consistently across phases, while low-rated systems spend relatively more turns evolving—possibly a deck-composition effect rather than a policy failure. That is exactly why we need the deck-controlled check below."},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"6a29c2cf","metadata":{},"source":"## 5 · Outcome lens: pressure matters more than a silver bullet Within each rating cohort, I compare won and lost games at the team level. Filled circles are high-rated systems; open squares are low-rated systems. The result is deliberately less cinematic than the Sankey: winners mostly differ in **converting more turns into attacks**, not in universally drawing or gusting more."},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":9,"id":"a5f0996b","metadata":{"execution":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.029829Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.029741Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.234395Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-08-02T00:05:28.233956Z"}},"outputs":[],"source":"outcome_metrics = ["has_draw", "has_search", "has_evolve", "has_attach", "has_gust", "has_attack"] ep = turns.groupby(["cohort", "team_id", "episode_id", "won"], as_index=False)[outcome_metrics].mean() team_outcome = ep.groupby(["cohort", "team_id", "won"], as_index=False)[outcome_metrics].mean() def outcome_delta(cohort, metric, seed=7, draws=10_000): pivot = team_outcome.query("cohort == @cohort").pivot(index="team_id", columns="won", values=metric).dropna() paired = (pivot[1] - pivot[0]).to_numpy() rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) sims = paired[rng.integers(0, len(paired), (draws, len(paired)))].mean(1) return paired.mean(), *np.quantile(sims, [.025, .975]) out = [] for cohort in ["high", "low"]: for metric in outcome_metrics: est, lo, hi = outcome_delta(cohort, metric, seed=19 + len(metric)) out.append({"cohort": cohort, "metric": metric, "estimate": est*100, "lo": lo*100, "hi": hi*100}) out = pd.DataFrame(out) labels_short = {**labels, "actions": "Actions / turn"} order = ["has_attack", "has_attach", "has_search", "has_draw", "has_evolve", "has_gust"] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6)) for cohort, color, marker, offset, fill in [ ("high", BLUE, "o", .13, BLUE), ("low", GOLD, "s", -.13, "white") ]: z = out.query("cohort == @cohort").set_index("metric").loc[order].reset_index() y = np.arange(len(order)) + offset ax.errorbar(z.estimate, y, xerr=[z.estimate-z.lo, z.hi-z.estimate], fmt=marker, markerfacecolor=fill, markeredgecolor=color, color=color, ecolor=color, capsize=3.5, lw=1.5, ms=7, label=f"{cohort.title()} rated") ax.axvline(0, color=INK, lw=1) ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(order)), [labels_short[x] for x in order]) ax.set_xlabel("Winners − losers (percentage points)") fig.suptitle("Within-cohort differences between won and lost games", x=.01, y=.98, ha="left", fontsize=17, weight="bold") fig.text(.01, .91, "Paired team means with 95% team-bootstrap intervals", color=MUTED, fontsize=10) ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1.11), ncol=2) ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False) ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False) fig.subplots_adjust(left=.22, right=.97, bottom=.14, top=.78) finish_mpl(fig, "05_outcome_forest", tight=False)"},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"aa9fa758","metadata":{},"source":"## 6 · The deck-confounding check Agent and deck are submitted together, so the headline comparison mixes policy, list construction, and matchup exposure.
